title: kv-cache: adaptive memory management and eviction + async spillover scheduling
author: Liam O'Connor
description: Motivation: Under heavy multi-tenant workloads we observed KV-cache fragmentation and frequent OOMs on long-lived GPU workers. This PR implements a set of coordinated features to reduce fragmentation, enable async spillover/paging to host memory, and introduce an eviction policy that accounts for both recency and token-weighted memory footprint. Summary of changes: 1) memory allocator: introduce a fragmentation-aware arena allocator with periodic lightweight compaction hooks that operate concurrently with inference (configurable compaction window). 2) spillover/paging: background async spillover to host pinned memory with oportunistic prefetch; pages are tracked by LRU epochs and can be rehydrated on hot-paths. 3) eviction policy: token-weighted LRU (TW-LRU) where entries score = alpha * recency_score + beta * (token_count / entry_size) and thresholds tuned per-model-profile. 4) scheduling: low-latency background compaction and spill threads with throttled CPU/GPU synchronization to avoid stalling the serving thread. 5) continuous batching integration: cache admission and eviction hooks added to batching pipeline so that large prefix reuse doesn't cause cache thrash across batches. 6) metrics + tracing: new metrics for fragmentation_ratio, spill_bytes, rehydrate_latency_p50/p90/p99, and eviction_reason histogram; traces include compaction span and spill/prefetch spans. Backwards compatibility: defaults maintain previous behavior; new behavior gated behind feature flag KV_CACHE_ADAPTIVE_V2 and per-deployment config in runtime profile. Testing: unit tests for allocator invariants and eviction scoring, integration tests with synthetic workloads (long-context multi-tenant replay) and end-to-end soak tests on staging GPU fleets. Benchmarks: - 27% reduction in peak GPU memory under mixed tenant workload (64 concurrent streams) - 12% median generation latency improvement for long-context traces (>= 8k tokens) due to reduced compaction pauses - Spillover rehydrate p90 under 8ms for typical hot-sets (measured on p4d-like instance). Rollout plan: gate flag off by default; enable in canary pool (10% workers) for 48h with detailed telemetry; increase to 50% after smoke checks; full rollout after one week if no regressions. Follow-ups: - auto-tune alpha/beta per workload (follow-up ENG-4729) - support optional compressed spill format (TODO). See linked Linear ENG-4582 for incident context and perf dashboards: link in Linear ticket. Checklist: - [x] allocator impl + unit tests - [x] async spill/prefetch + integration tests - [x] eviction policy + tuning harness - [x] batching integration + tests - [x] metrics + dashboard patches - [x] e2e soak tests on staging - [x] docs update (runtime docs + config reference)

merge_commit_message:
kv-cache: adaptive memory management + async spillover + TW-LRU eviction

Introduce fragmentation-aware allocator, async spill/prefetch to host memory, token-weighted LRU eviction policy, batching hooks and telemetry. Gate behind KV_CACHE_ADAPTIVE_V2 flag.

Benchmarks: -27% peak GPU memory (mixed load), +12% median latency for long-contexts.

Linked: ENG-4582
release_notes: Runtime: Improved KV cache memory management — fragmentation-aware allocator, async spillover to host memory, and token-weighted eviction policy. Feature gated behind KV_CACHE_ADAPTIVE_V2. Reduces peak GPU memory and lowers long-context latency for many workloads.
